area: Embodied navigation: ObjectNav / open-vocabulary ObjectNav, Instance-ImageNav, VLN-CE, lifelong multi-goal (GOAT), EQA-style exploration, navigation VLAs and world models, legged-robot VLN, social navigation, sim-to-real

papers.title: VLFM: Vision-Language Frontier Maps for Zero-Shot Semantic Navigation
papers.key_idea: Scores each RGB frame against the target text with a pre-trained VLM (BLIP-2 ITM via LAVIS) to build a language-grounded value map, then heads for the highest-value frontier. GroundingDINO, YOLOv7 and MobileSAM confirm the goal. Deployed zero-shot on a real Boston Dynamics Spot.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free apart from a supplied PointNav policy. Models are served locally via Flask and fit one 8 GB GPU. SR/SPL (ApexNav table): HM3Dv1 52.5/30.4, HM3Dv2 63.6/32.5, MP3D 36.4/17.5. Pinned to torch 1.12+cu113, so it must be rebuilt for RTX 50-series.
papers.limitation: One image-text similarity score gives only shallow semantics, with no relational or common-sense reasoning. Detector false positives cause wrong stops. Still the baseline every zero-shot ObjectNav paper compares against.

papers.title: SG-Nav: Online 3D Scene Graph Prompting for LLM-based Zero-shot Object Navigation
papers.key_idea: Builds an online 3D scene graph during exploration and prompts an LLM with hierarchical chain-of-thought over subgraphs, producing explainable estimates of how likely the goal is near each frontier. Training-free across scenes and categories.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free: local open-vocab perception plus LLM calls (API or local). 8 GB is enough if the LLM is remote or small. SR/SPL (ApexNav table): HM3Dv1 54.0/24.9, MP3D 40.2/16.0.
papers.limitation: LLM latency and cost on every step. Graph quality is capped by detector noise. Text-only edges throw away visual detail, which motivated MSGNav. Evaluated mostly in simulation.

papers.title: InstructNav: Zero-shot System for Generic Instruction Navigation in Unexplored Environment
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2406.04882 (2024; often cited as CoRL 2024, not verified)
papers.key_idea: Dynamic Chain-of-Navigation (DCoN) runs one LLM-driven planning process across many instruction-navigation task types, using RGB-D and pose in unexplored continuous environments. No navigation training and no prebuilt map.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free: GPT-class API reasoning plus local perception, so an 8 GB GPU is enough. HM3Dv2 ObjectNav 58.0/20.9 SR/SPL (ApexNav table).
papers.limitation: arXiv 2507.20021 ('When Engineering Outruns Intelligence') finds that a purely geometric frontier explorer with zero API calls matches or beats detector-controlled InstructNav on HM3D/MP3D. Much of the gain is engineering, not language.

papers.title: UniGoal: Towards Universal Zero-shot Goal-oriented Navigation
papers.key_idea: Converts object-category, instance-image and text goals into one goal-graph form. At each step it matches the goal graph against an online scene graph, and the matching score drives a multi-stage exploration policy. One training-free model handles ObjectNav, Instance-ImageNav and TextNav.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. Uses SAM ViT-H, GroundingDINO, LightGlue and faiss-gpu, plus an LLM/VLM via Ollama (llama3.2-vision) or an API. A local VLM together with SAM-H probably won't fit in 8 GB, so use the API backend. habitat-sim 0.2.3, Python 3.8 (same as the system Python).
papers.code: https://github.com/bagh2178/UniGoal (MIT; real-robot env stub to implement)
papers.limitation: Building and matching graphs every step is slow. The README confirms IIN/TextNav code, but the ObjectNav release was only announced. You must write the real-robot step/pose interface yourself.

papers.title: ApexNav: An Adaptive Exploration Strategy for Zero-Shot Object Navigation with Target-centric Semantic Fusion
papers.venue_year: IEEE RA-L 2025 (accepted Aug 2025; journal, not CCF-A)
papers.key_idea: Uses semantic reasoning to explore when semantic cues are strong and switches to geometric frontier exploration when they are weak. Target-centric fusion keeps long-term memory of the target and similar-looking objects to suppress false detections.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free: YOLOv7, GroundingDINO, MobileSAM and BLIP-2, plus DeepSeek-V3 for priors. The real robot was driven from an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (8 GB), a direct match for this hardware. SR/SPL: HM3Dv1 59.6/33.0, HM3Dv2 76.2/38.0, MP3D 39.2/17.8.
papers.limitation: Real-world validation is only 6 trials on a wheeled AgileX LIMO. On the laptop, detection overruns its 250 ms budget. LLM priors are fixed per category. Supports object-category goals only.

papers.title: WMNav: Integrating Vision-Language Models into World Models for Object Goal Navigation
papers.key_idea: Treats a VLM as a world model that predicts what each candidate direction leads to, and stores those predictions in an online Curiosity Value Map. Adds subtask decomposition and a two-stage action proposer (explore, then localize), with plan-vs-observation feedback to curb hallucination.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. Uses the Gemini API (main results) or local Qwen2.5-VL via vLLM. Habitat needs about 320 MB of GPU memory per episode. SR/SPL with Gemini 1.5 Pro: HM3D 58.1/31.2, MP3D 45.4/17.2. With local Qwen2.5-VL-7B it drops to 46.1/20.7, and with 3B to 29.7/15.8.
papers.limitation: No real-robot experiments. Relies on a proprietary cloud VLM. Several VLM calls per step add latency.

papers.title: CogNav: Cognitive Process Modeling for Object Goal Navigation with LLMs
papers.key_idea: Models ObjectNav as a finite-state machine of cognitive states, from exploration to identification. An LLM chooses state transitions by reasoning over an online heterogeneous cognitive map that holds spatial and semantic information. Claims at least 14% relative SR gain on HM3D, MP3D and RoboTHOR.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free LLM reasoning plus local mapping and perception. 8 GB is enough for perception if the LLM is remote. The abstract doesn't name the LLM.
papers.limitation: The state set is hand-designed, and LLM calls add latency. The abstract page gives no per-benchmark numbers and no robot details.

papers.title: MSGNav: Unleashing the Power of Multi-modal 3D Scene Graph for Zero-Shot Embodied Navigation
papers.key_idea: A multi-modal 3D scene graph whose relation edges are dynamically assigned images instead of text. Modules: key-subgraph selection, adaptive vocabulary update, closed-loop reasoning, and visibility-based final-viewpoint choice for the 'last mile'. Evaluated on GOAT-Bench and HM3D-ObjNav.
papers.compute_needs: Zero-shot, with no task-specific training. VLM-heavy, since image edges raise the token count (the VLM isn't named on the abstract page). Practical on 8 GB only with an API or a small local VLM.
papers.code: https://github.com/ylwhxht/MSGNav (HM3D eval bug fixed Mar 2026; Unitree G1 deployment 'coming soon')
papers.limitation: High VLM token cost. An HM3D evaluation-code bug means published numbers need careful comparison. No quadruped results yet.

papers.title: TrajRAG: Retrieving Geometric-Semantic Experience for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
papers.key_idea: Retrieval-augmented ObjectNav. Past trajectories are stored in a compact topo-polar form and grouped by hierarchical chunking. Each frontier generates trajectory hypotheses, which are matched against the stored experience to guide LLM/VLM waypoint choice. The store is consolidated over a lifetime. Evaluated on MP3D and HM3D-v1/v2.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. The retrieval store is light on CPU and RAM. Large-model reasoning (models not named on the abstract page) can run via API or locally. One 8 GB GPU looks workable.
papers.limitation: Gains depend on how similar new environments are to stored experience. The abstract page gives no numbers. Not tested on legged robots.

papers.title: 3D-Mem: 3D Scene Memory for Embodied Exploration and Reasoning
papers.key_idea: Stores explored space as multi-view 'Memory Snapshots' and unexplored space as 'Frontier Snapshots', so a VLM can weigh known against unknown regions for EQA and lifelong navigation. Uses incremental construction and memory retrieval in place of object-centric scene graphs.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free with a large VLM (not named on the abstract page). Snapshot images inflate VLM tokens, so 8 GB works only with an API or a small VLM.
papers.limitation: Image memory and token cost grow with scene size. Simulation-centric. Serves as the common baseline for EQA and GOAT-style follow-ups.

papers.title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
papers.key_idea: Two-level legged VLN. A VLA (SigLIP + LLaMA3-8B, built on NVILA/VILA) outputs mid-level language actions such as 'move forward 75 cm', and a LiDAR-based RL locomotion policy executes them while avoiding obstacles. Real-world runs on Unitree Go2, G1 and Booster T1; introduces the VLN-CE-Isaac benchmark.
papers.compute_needs: SFT scripts assume multiple GPUs. The 8B model is about 16 GB in bf16, so one 8 GB GPU needs 4-bit inference, and QLoRA would be tight. SR/SPL: R2R-CE 54.0/49.0, RxR-CE 49.3/44.0 (DualVLN table). Stack: Habitat 0.1.7, CUDA 12.2, torch 2.3.
papers.code: https://github.com/AnjieCheng/NaVILA (Apache-2.0; plus legged-loco and NaVILA-Bench repos)
papers.limitation: Mid-level actions are coarse and issued at a low rate. The locomotion policy needs LiDAR. You have to download the YouTube training videos yourself. RSS is not a CCF venue.

papers.title: Uni-NaVid: A Video-based Vision-Language-Action Model for Unifying Embodied Navigation Tasks
papers.key_idea: A single video VLA (EVA-CLIP + Vicuna-7B, building on LLaMA-VID/NaVid) with online visual token merging. It unifies VLN, ObjectNav, EQA and human following, outputs discrete actions, and was trained on 3.6M samples. Deployed zero-shot in the real world.
papers.compute_needs: Training needs multiple GPUs. Inference runs at about 5 Hz on one A100. 7B in fp16 is about 14 GB, so 8 GB needs 4-bit. SR/SPL: R2R-CE 47.0/42.7, RxR-CE 48.7/40.9 (DualVLN table; the README reports 51.8/47.7 on R2R).
papers.limitation: Discrete actions and no explicit 3D memory. Data-hungry. ObjectNav imitation data was left out of the release for licensing reasons.

papers.title: StreamVLN: Streaming Vision-and-Language Navigation via SlowFast Context Modeling
papers.key_idea: A Video-LLM built on LLaVA-Video. A fast sliding-window dialogue context reuses the KV cache, and a slow memory is compressed with 3D-aware token pruning, which keeps both context and latency bounded on long streams.
papers.compute_needs: Multi-GPU SFT on about 450K oracle clips, 240K DAgger samples, and VQA/MMC4 data. The 7B-class backbone (size not verified) needs quantization to fit 8 GB. SR/SPL: R2R-CE 56.9/51.9, RxR-CE 52.9/46.0.
papers.limitation: RGB-only with discrete actions. Since surpassed by DualVLN and Efficient-VLN. The project page doesn't name the real robot or its compute.

papers.title: Ground Slow, Move Fast: A Dual-System Foundation Model for Generalizable Vision-and-Language Navigation (DualVLN / InternVLA-N1)
papers.venue_year: ICLR 2026 (not in CCF AI A list)
papers.key_idea: System 2 is Qwen2.5-VL-7B and predicts pixel goals at about 2 Hz. System 1 is a compact flow-matching DiT that generates 32 waypoints at about 30 Hz from RGB plus pixel and latent goals. The two run asynchronously. Deployed on Turtlebot4, Unitree Go2 and Unitree G1.
papers.compute_needs: Real-robot setup used an offboard RTX 4090 at about 20 GB. S1 runs in 0.03 s with TensorRT. On 8 GB, S2 has to be 4-bit or run offboard. SR/SPL: R2R-CE 64.3/58.5, RxR-CE 61.4/51.8. VLN-PE physical-controller SR is 51.6.
papers.limitation: Data-heavy, and InternData-N1 is CC BY-NC-SA. S2 has a large memory footprint. On VLN-PE, SR falls from 63.6 to 51.6 when the flash controller is replaced by the physical one.

papers.title: Embodied Navigation Foundation Model (NavFoM)
papers.key_idea: A cross-embodiment, cross-task navigation model trained on about 8M samples from quadrupeds, drones, wheeled robots and cars. Identifier tokens encode the camera setup and the task horizon, and adaptive token sampling keeps a fixed token budget. Covers VLN, object search, tracking and driving.
papers.compute_needs: Training is cluster-scale. The arXiv page links no weights, so 8 GB allows at most evaluation, and only if weights are released and quantized.
papers.limitation: The data and compute are out of reach for small labs. The abstract gives no benchmark specifics. Venue unknown.

papers.title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.key_idea: Lifts CLIP features from posed RGB-D into patch, instance and zone 3D tokens that are updated online layer by layer, and feeds them to a 3D-VLM for action prediction. Supports pre-exploration, lifelong memory and dynamic scenes. Reports SOTA monocular results on R2R-CE, REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE, plus real-robot tests.
papers.compute_needs: Needs large-scale 3D-language pretraining plus task fine-tuning on multiple GPUs. Inference needs depth and pose. The backbone size isn't on the abstract page.
papers.limitation: Sensitive to pose and depth quality, which suffers from camera jitter on legged robots. Pretraining is far too heavy for one 8 GB GPU.

papers.title: Aux-Think: Exploring Reasoning Strategies for Data-Efficient Vision-Language Navigation
papers.key_idea: A systematic comparison of No-Think, Pre-Think and Post-Think for VLN finds 'Inference-time Reasoning Collapse': chain-of-thought at test time hurts. Aux-Think uses CoT only as auxiliary training supervision and acts without it at inference. Releases R2R-CoT-320k and claims Pareto data efficiency against Uni-NaVid and NaVILA.
papers.compute_needs: Requires VLM SFT; the GPU scale isn't on the abstract page. The recipe is cheap to reproduce with LoRA on a 2-3B VLM in 8 GB.
papers.limitation: VLN-CE simulation only. CoT labels come from large models. Not tested on legged embodiments.

papers.title: Navigation World Models
papers.key_idea: A 1B-parameter Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) predicts future egocentric frames from past frames and navigation actions. Trained on robot video plus unlabeled human egocentric video. Plans by cross-entropy-method search over imagined rollouts, or ranks trajectories proposed by external policies.
papers.compute_needs: The reference training run uses 64 GPUs. CDiT-XL weights fit in 8 GB for inference, but CEM planning (120 samples, each needing diffusion steps) is slow on one GPU.
papers.limitation: Image goals only, with no language or semantics. Planning is slow. Non-commercial license. Generated frames can hallucinate.

papers.title: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
papers.venue_year: 2024 (arXiv 2310.07896; usually cited as ICRA 2024, not verified)
papers.key_idea: One transformer with a diffusion action head. Masking the goal switches it between undirected exploration and image-goal navigation. Successor to the ViNT/GNM general navigation models trained on multi-robot data, and a standard local-policy baseline in InternNav and NavDP.
papers.compute_needs: A small model: inference and fine-tuning fit easily on one 8 GB GPU. Code and pretrained checkpoints are released.
papers.limitation: No language or semantic goals. Without a goal image or topological map it explores aimlessly in unseen spaces, as ODG-NoMaD points out.

papers.title: NavDP: Learning Sim-to-Real Navigation Diffusion Policy with Privileged Information Guidance
papers.key_idea: One transformer both generates trajectories (by diffusion) and scores them (with a critic) from local RGB-D. Trained only in simulation, using privileged global information for demonstrations and contrastive negatives. Real-to-sim data adds about 30% SR. Transfers zero-shot across embodiments and serves as the InternVLA-N1 System 1.
papers.compute_needs: Inference is light and fits 8 GB. Training relies on large amounts of sim-generated data; single-GPU fine-tuning looks plausible. SR/SPL: ClutteredEnv 89.8/87.7, InternScenes 65.7/60.7.
papers.limitation: Handles only local point and image goals, with no semantics. Needs RGB-D. X-NavDP (arXiv 2607.28560) shows hard real-world cases at only 10% SR before online RL fine-tuning.

papers.title: Rethinking the Embodied Gap in Vision-and-Language Navigation: A Holistic Study of Physical and Visual Disparities (VLN-PE)
papers.key_idea: A physically realistic VLN platform for humanoid, quadruped and wheeled robots. Tests discrete-action, diffusion-waypoint and training-free LLM+map pipelines, and finds large drops from limited robot viewpoints, lighting changes, collisions and falls, along with limits of legged locomotion.
papers.compute_needs: Mainly an evaluation work. The physics simulator, run through InternNav on Isaac Sim, is heavier than Habitat, so 8 GB may limit scene complexity.
papers.limitation: Diagnoses the gap but doesn't propose a fix. Scenes are mostly MP3D-derived. The physics is simulated, not a real robot.

papers.title: Ground-level Viewpoint Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (GVNav)
papers.key_idea: Tackles the mismatch between instructions and training views at human height and the low camera on a quadruped. Weighted historical observations resolve feature collisions, and connectivity graphs transferred from HM3D/Gibson strengthen waypoint prediction. Validated on real quadrupeds.
papers.compute_needs: A conventional VLN-CE waypoint-predictor model. Single-GPU training seems plausible, but the paper doesn't say.
papers.limitation: Tied to the waypoint-predictor pipeline. The abstract gives no metrics and doesn't name the quadruped.

papers.title: EmbodiedSplat: Personalized Real-to-Sim-to-Real Navigation with Gaussian Splats from a Mobile Device
papers.key_idea: Captures the deployment space with an iPhone, reconstructs a mesh with 3D Gaussian Splatting, loads it into Habitat-Sim, and fine-tunes ImageNav policies in the replica. Real-world SR rises by 20 points over HM3D-pretrained and 40 points over HSSD-pretrained policies. Sim-real correlation is 0.87-0.97.
papers.compute_needs: 3DGS reconstruction plus Habitat fine-tuning is plausible at consumer-GPU scale, though the abstract page doesn't state fine-tuning compute.
papers.limitation: ImageNav only, with static scenes. Each environment needs its own capture. The abstract page doesn't name the robot.

papers.title: History-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation
papers.key_idea: A training-free plug-in for VLA-based VLN. Selects spatial tokens from the current view and compresses history spatio-temporally, using attention-based importance and query-guided filtering. Keeps accuracy under extreme pruning, and shows low-latency instruction following on a Unitree Go2.
papers.compute_needs: Training-free. Cuts latency and visual-token memory of navigation VLAs, which bears directly on 8 GB deployment.
papers.limitation: The abstract page names neither the base VLA nor any numbers. Pruning doesn't shrink the 7B weight footprint. IROS is not CCF-A.

papers.title: VLN-R1: Vision-Language Navigation via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
papers.key_idea: An LVLM maps egocentric video directly to continuous navigation actions. Training runs in two stages: SFT, then GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning with a Time-Decayed Reward over multi-step future actions, plus Long-Short Memory Sampling. Introduces the VLN-Ego dataset built in Habitat.
papers.compute_needs: Needs SFT plus GRPO on an LVLM (base size not verified). RFT on a small 2-3B VLM with LoRA might fit in 8 GB, but group rollouts in Habitat are slow.
papers.limitation: The abstract gives no VLN-CE numbers. Rewards are sparse and episode-level, which later step-level reward work addresses. Simulation only.

benchmarks.name: HM3D ObjectNav (v1 = HM3D v0.1, 2000 val episodes; v2 = HM3D v0.2, 1000 val episodes)
benchmarks.sota_note: Best training-free results: ApexNav 59.6/33.0 on v1 and 76.2/38.0 on v2, and WMNav 58.1/31.2 on v1. The trained OVRL-V2 gets 64.7/28.1 on v1. Some 2026 arXiv papers claim more (HAM-VLN 79.7 SR on v2, a fast-slow ReAct agent 68.75 SR on v1), but these aren't peer-reviewed yet.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Habitat itself is light, about 320 MB GPU per episode (WMNav README). 8 GB holds detector, SAM and BLIP-2 perception for 1-2 parallel envs. Run the LLM/VLM through an API or quantize it locally.

benchmarks.name: MP3D ObjectNav
benchmarks.sota_note: Training-free: WMNav 45.4/17.2, SG-Nav 40.2/16.0, ApexNav 39.2/17.8. Its meshes are noisier, so it's harder than HM3D.

benchmarks.name: HM3D-OVON (open-vocabulary ObjectNav)
benchmarks.simulator: Habitat on HM3DSem: 379 categories, more than 15k object instances
benchmarks.metrics: SR, SPL (val-unseen is the headline split)
benchmarks.sota_note: OVSegDT (arXiv 2508.11479) reports 44.7 SR / 20.6 SPL on val-unseen without depth, odometry or large VLMs. MerNav (arXiv 2602.05467) reports +6% SR zero-shot, and FSUNav also evaluates on it. The benchmark paper (arXiv 2409.14296) has no verified venue.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Habitat evaluation fits 8 GB. Training RL agents from scratch is not realistic on one GPU.

benchmarks.name: GOAT-Bench (multi-modal lifelong navigation)
benchmarks.simulator: Habitat (HM3D), with sequential goals given as a category, a language description or an instance image
benchmarks.metrics: Subtask SR, SPL over multi-goal episodes
benchmarks.sota_note: The modular GOAT baseline gets 24.9% subtask SR on val-unseen. 2026 arXiv results: AnyGoal 52.4 SR / 12.7 SPL under the strict physical regime with no teleport, STEGNav 66.3 SR / 39.7 SPL, SoftNav 67.2 SR. Their settings differ. MSGNav (CVPR 2026) and 3D-Mem (CVPR 2025) also evaluate here.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Training-free agents run on 8 GB with an API VLM. Episodes are long, so evaluation takes a lot of time.

benchmarks.name: R2R-CE / RxR-CE (VLN-CE)
benchmarks.simulator: Habitat on MP3D scenes (the VLN-CE stack uses habitat-sim 0.1.7)
benchmarks.metrics: SR, SPL, NE, OSR; nDTW for RxR
benchmarks.sota_note: Trained RGB models on val-unseen: DualVLN 64.3/58.5 (R2R) and 61.4/51.8 (RxR), StreamVLN 56.9/51.9, NaVILA 54.0/49.0. Efficient-VLN v2 claims 73.2/75.6 SR (arXiv only). Zero-shot: HAM-VLN 61.0 SR, SparseNav 42.8 SR. Many zero-shot papers report on 100-episode subsets, so the numbers aren't comparable.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Evaluating a 7-8B VLA needs about 16 GB in bf16, or 4-bit quantization to fit 8 GB. Zero-shot API agents need little GPU.

benchmarks.name: Instance-ImageNav / TextNav (HM3D)
benchmarks.simulator: Habitat (HM3D; UniGoal uses the HM3D v3 instance-imagenav val episodes)
benchmarks.sota_note: UniGoal (CVPR 2025) is the training-free universal reference. The 2023 modular IIN baseline reached 56% SR. 'Any-View Geometry' (arXiv 2604.05351) claims 82.6% image-goal SR on HM3D, but the exact task variant is unclear.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Training-free pipelines with SAM-H and LightGlue fit 8 GB if the LLM runs remotely.

benchmarks.name: VLN-PE / VLN-CE-Isaac (physically realistic VLN)
benchmarks.simulator: Isaac Sim-based (InternNav / NaVILA-Bench), with humanoid, quadruped and wheeled robots
benchmarks.metrics: SR, SPL, NE, OSR, plus falls and collisions
benchmarks.sota_note: On VLN-PE R2R unseen, DualVLN gets 63.6 SR with the flash controller and 51.6 with the physical controller. The classic RDP gets about 25.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Isaac Sim rendering is much heavier than Habitat. 8 GB is at the low end, so check Isaac Sim's requirements.

benchmarks.name: OpenEQA (A-EQA) / EXPRESS-Bench (EQA-style exploration)
benchmarks.metrics: LLM-Match answer score plus efficiency-weighted or visually grounded SPL
benchmarks.sota_note: 3D-Mem (CVPR 2025) is the common baseline. Step-Level Calibration (arXiv 2511.19768) reports up to 49% relative gain in grounded SPL and 33% in LLM-Match.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Training-free with an API VLM. 8 GB is enough for mapping and detection.

benchmarks.name: Social / human-aware navigation (HA-VLN 2.0, LISN-Bench, SocialNav-SUB)
benchmarks.simulator: HA-VLN 2.0 covers discrete and continuous settings with dynamic multi-human scenes. LISN-Bench runs on Rosnav-Arena 3.0. SocialNav-SUB is VQA.
benchmarks.metrics: SR plus collision and social-compliance rates; VQA accuracy
benchmarks.sota_note: The LISN-Bench VLM-modulated controller reaches 91.3% average success. SocialNav-SUB and arXiv 2609.40245 find VLMs still trail rule-based methods and human consensus on social understanding. I found no legged-specific social-nav benchmark.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Mostly light. The VQA benchmarks run on any GPU.

benchmarks.name: Real-to-sim 3DGS evaluation (EmbodiedSplat, POINav-Bench)
benchmarks.simulator: 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions converted to Habitat meshes or closed-loop renderers
benchmarks.metrics: Real-vs-sim SR correlation; SR on reconstructed real scenes
benchmarks.sota_note: EmbodiedSplat gets 0.87-0.97 sim-real correlation and +20 to +40 points real SR after fine-tuning. POINav-Bench reconstructs 11 commercial areas (about 126k m², 163 POIs) for closed-loop last-meters VLN.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Reconstructing a room or floor with 3DGS is usually feasible on one consumer GPU.

trends: Real robots now default to a dual system: a slow VLM planner plus a fast local policy. Examples: DualVLN/InternVLA-N1 (2 Hz VLM, 30 Hz DiT), NaVILA (VLA plus RL locomotion), FSUNav's cerebrum-cerebellum design (arXiv 2604.03139), and SysNav, a three-tier system that calls the VLM at room level on Go2 and G1 (arXiv 2603.06914).

Efficiency is now publishable at CCF-A in its own right. Examples: streaming KV-cache reuse (StreamVLN, Efficient-VLN), training-free token pruning (IROS 2026, on Go2), Input-Adaptive VLN (ICCV 2025, more than 2x compute cut), and COSMO low-cost VLN (ICCV 2025).

Training-free ObjectNav is maturing through richer memory: 3D scene graphs (SG-Nav, UniGoal, MSGNav), the VLM as a world model (WMNav), cognitive FSMs (CogNav), experience retrieval (TrajRAG, CVPR 2026), and Gaussian-language maps (GLMap, CVPR 2026). HM3Dv2 SR is now above 75%.

Navigation VLMs are getting RL post-training with GRPO: VLN-R1, MobileVLA-R1 (continuous quadruped control, about 5% gain), ETP-R1, SeeNav-Agent with step-level rewards, and step-aware contrastive alignment. The central problems are sparse outcome rewards and errors that compound after SFT.

General frontier models in thin agent harnesses now match or beat trained VLN policies. Examples: AgenticNav tool-calling (arXiv 2606.10577, 76% SR, split unstated), 'Embodied Agents Take Control' (arXiv 2607.26148), and a GPT-6-Astra tech report claiming 81.3% SR on R2R-CE-100. These often use 100-episode subsets.

More work is testing claims against reality. VLN-PE (ICCV 2025) and GVNav (ICRA 2025) measure drops from low viewpoints, lighting, collisions and falls. 'When Engineering Outruns Intelligence' finds frontier geometry explains most zero-shot ObjectNav gains. Expect more evaluation-centric papers.

Data scale is concentrating in big labs: NavFoM (8M samples), Uni-NaVid (3.6M), TrackVLA (1.7M), InternData-N1. Small labs contribute plug-ins, evaluation protocols, and efficient adaptation of released checkpoints instead.

Real-to-sim with 3D Gaussian Splatting is used for personalized fine-tuning and closed-loop evaluation in real scenes: EmbodiedSplat (ICCV 2025), POINav-Bench, ReaDy-Go (dynamic 3DGS with moving obstacles), and a photorealistic 3DGS social-nav platform (arXiv 2607.25219).

Two sub-areas are growing. Lifelong multi-goal memory on GOAT-Bench: 3D-Mem, AnyGoal's multi-agent Bayesian value map, STEGNav's event graphs. Human-aware and language-constrained social navigation: HA-VLN 2.0, LISN-Bench.
open_gaps: Cloud-to-local reasoning gap. On HM3D, WMNav drops from 58.1 SR with Gemini 1.5 Pro to 46.1 with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 29.7 with 3B. C2Nav gets 31.0 SR with Qwen3-VL-8B against 44.0 with GPT-5.5. Making local VLMs of 8B or less navigate well on 8 GB is still open.

Legged-specific perception. Low camera height, gait-induced shake and blur, pitch oscillation and odometry drift on quadrupeds have been diagnosed (GVNav, VLN-PE). Zero-shot ObjectNav/VLN pipelines rarely model them and still assume a stable wheeled-robot camera at a fixed height.

Latency-aware asynchronous decisions. VLM planners run at 1-2 Hz (DualVLN's S2 takes 0.7-1.1 s) while a legged robot keeps moving. When to call the VLM, how to compensate for stale plans, and how to budget calls (SysNav calls at room level) haven't been studied systematically.

Goal verification and stopping. AnyGoal finds that open-vocabulary detectors move the main failure from exploration to goal verification. ApexNav's fusion is heuristic, and MSGNav addresses last-mile viewpoints. Calibrated, uncertainty-aware stop and verify decisions for open-vocabulary targets remain unsolved.

Evaluation hygiene. Zero-shot VLN-CE results often come from 100-episode subsets, success thresholds vary, GOAT-Bench numbers mix teleport and strict-physical regimes, and MSGNav had to fix an HM3D evaluation bug. A reproducible protocol with a real-quadruped test suite would be valuable.

Language versus geometry. Simple frontier geometry matches LLM planners (arXiv 2507.20021). There's still no principled account of when language or common-sense priors actually help, for example in large multi-room buildings, with ambiguous or relational goals, or in multi-floor search.

Real-to-sim for legged robots with semantic goals. EmbodiedSplat shows big real-world gains for ImageNav. Extending phone-captured 3DGS replicas to quadruped dynamics, language and object goals, and moving people is still open; ReaDy-Go is an early step.
Real-world lifelong memory. GOAT-style lifelong benchmarks are simulated with static scenes. Compact, updatable memory that survives days of scene change on one robot with 32 GB RAM is underexplored.
Quadruped social navigation. VLMs trail rule-based methods on social understanding (SocialNav-SUB; arXiv 2609.40245), and this sweep found no legged-robot social-nav benchmark.
low_compute_entry_points: Fork ApexNav or VLFM. Both are training-free, and ApexNav already drives a real robot from an 8 GB RTX 4060 Laptop. Add one module (calibrated goal verification, gait-aware stabilization, or VLM-call scheduling) and report full HM3Dv1/v2 and MP3D splits plus 30 or more real M1 trials.

Cloud-to-local distillation. Log a cloud teacher's frontier scores and stop/verify decisions on HM3D train scenes (if an API is available). QLoRA-tune a VLM around 3B (Qwen2.5-VL-3B class) on 8 GB, using CoT only as training supervision, following Aux-Think. Report how much of the gap to WMNav's local results closes.

Plug-in efficiency for released navigation VLAs (NaVILA-8B, Uni-NaVid-7B, InternVLA-N1): 4-bit weights plus training-free token pruning and KV reuse. Measure R2R-CE/RxR-CE accuracy against latency on the 5060 and on the robot. Efficiency work does get into ICCV (Input-Adaptive VLN).

Study and fix the quadruped embodiment gap. In Habitat, vary camera height, tilt, shake and blur to mimic the M1's gait, and reproduce VLN-PE/GVNav-style drops for 3-4 zero-shot methods. Then propose a light fix, such as viewpoint-adaptive features or temporal fusion, and validate it on the M1.

Build a phone-captured 3DGS replica of your lab or building, following the EmbodiedSplat recipe. Use it to fine-tune a small local policy (NavDP/NoMaD class) and as a real-to-sim evaluation set, with a sim-real correlation analysis for the quadruped.

Run a dual system on a budget. Keep a frozen, quantized VLM planner on the 5060 desktop (DualVLN also streams RGB-D to an offboard GPU). Train or fine-tune only a small System-1 local policy (NavDP/NoMaD scale) for the M1's dynamics in simulation.

Robot integration. The M1 needs a velocity-command API (vx, vy, yaw rate), odometry, and an RGB-D camera; DualVLN used a RealSense D455 tilted 15 degrees down. Stream to the desktop over Wi-Fi. InternNav's Go2 deployment code and UniGoal's real_world_env stub are good templates.

Software environment. Ubuntu 20.04 with Python 3.8 is too old for most stacks, so use Docker or conda per repo: UniGoal needs Py3.8 + habitat-sim 0.2.3, WMNav Py3.9 + habitat-sim 0.3.1, NaVILA Py3.10 + Habitat 0.1.7. The RTX 5060 (sm_120) generally needs PyTorch built for CUDA 12.8 or later; cu113/cu121 wheels won't run natively.
ccf_venue_note: From the ccf.org.cn AI list (fetched): CCF-A conferences are AAAI, NeurIPS, ACL, CVPR, ICCV, ICML and IJCAI. ICRA and ECCV are CCF-B. IROS, RSS, CoRL and ICLR are not in the AI A list. A third-party 2026 list (unverified) has TPAMI and IJCV as A journals and T-RO as B. Many navigation papers appear at ICRA, IROS, RA-L or RSS, none of which count as CCF-A, so aim for CVPR, ICCV, NeurIPS, AAAI or IJCAI.
